steps.label: How Anytime Soccer Training Is Structured
steps.text:
Before we get to where to start, let's go over how Anytime Soccer Training is put together.

**📋 How training is organized**

• **All Programs** — all skill areas grouped by programs.

• **Curated Curriculum** — programs organized in a recommended order.

• **Custom Folders and Favorites** — create your own video folders.

• **Recurring Training Plans** — recurring sessions that auto update.

We will cover each — pick what fits you best.

On day one, we recommend starting with ball mastery.

• It's one of the most important skills you can learn.

• You don't need any equipment.

• You can do it in your living room, your garage, or out on the field.

Here are a few ball mastery programs to get you started.
steps.label: Start with Ball Mastery

player.q: Do you recommend a training plan?

steps.label: Yes — But It Depends on Your Preference
steps.text:
Training plans are recurring and give you a guided path.

• However, some users prefer sticking with a few folders and working through them at their own pace.

• I use both.

• I built a custom plan for my son's after-school training, and I favorite folders we use for longer training sessions.

player.q: How long should my child train?

steps.label: The Key to Success: Train at a Level They Can Stick With
steps.text:
We call this **MEEE** — the Minimum Extra Effort they can do with Enthusiasm.

A few things to keep in mind:

• Consistency beats intensity — even **20 minutes a week** can meaningfully improve a player's skill

• Sit down with your child and set a weekly goal together, one they can realistically handle

• Let them help pick the goal — a goal they chose is a goal they'll keep

steps.label: No — With a Few Exceptions
steps.text:
The program stacks skills — one new move per video, each building on the last.

• **INTRO** — teaches a new move

• **QR** — quick review of recent moves

• **FR** — full review of a block

Reviews bring back earlier moves automatically, so your child can train on their own without you having to manage or re-teach anything. Skip a video, though, and later reviews may reference a move they missed.

**Exceptions:**

• Strong jugglers can skip the early juggling build-up

• No space/equipment? Skip and return later

player.q: Where do beginners and experienced players start?

steps.label: Everyone Starts in the Same Place
steps.text:
We recommend all players start with the first folders and follow the program in order.

• The difference between experienced players and beginners is in the levels of **volume, variety, and variations**.

steps.label: Beginner
steps.text: A beginner may start with only the 1,000 Touch Ball Mastery program.

steps.label: Experienced
steps.text: An experienced player can handle multiple ball mastery programs, as well as training programs in other skill areas.
This is just one example. A beginner may focus on one type of ball mastery, where an experienced player should do several types — while still following them in order.

steps.label: Same Start, More Volume and Variety
steps.text:
As mentioned before, experienced players should still start with the first folders — what changes is how much they take on and how quickly they add to it.

• Another way to accelerate that variety is our **30-Day Plans**

• Each video works four to six different moves

• A player covers far more ground in the same session

Training is organized by skill areas, programs, and folders — the folders house the videos. For example, **Ball Mastery** is a skill area, **1,000 Touch** is a program, and **P1:** is the first folder.

**Types of folders**

• **All Programs** — lists every folder in each respective program.

• **Curated Curriculum** — folders by skill area, in our recommended order (rotates programs for variety).

• **30-Day Plans** — 30-day plans by skill area.

• **Favorites** — your own folders (add videos in Key Skills).

Training plans are recurring plans that you set and forget.

**Types of plans**

• **Weekly Plan** — organizes the skill videos by day, delivering skill areas into each day automatically.

• **30-Day Monthly Plan** — a weekly plan built from the 30-Day folders.

• **Custom Plan** — weekly videos based on the folders you pick yourself.

Many parents need a reminder. To send one, follow these steps:

• Go to New Player Onboard.

• Click **Send Reminder**.

• The reminder only goes to players who have not joined yet.

• Players who already have accounts are added to the team automatically.

Before or after practice, show the app and make sure everyone knows how to access their homework.

**A few tips**

• Ask a team manager for help.

• Gather feedback, and contact us with any questions.

• Bring a bluetooth speaker and have the team do a ball mastery video at training. It's fun!

Set your team's training goal for each period.

**A few tips**

• You can set the team goal for everyone at once.

• This goal appears on the roster.

• You can also set an individual goal.

A recurring challenge that keeps players motivated.

**How it works**

• Set the target: how many videos players need to complete.

• Pick the date it ends.

• Add a prize for the ultimate champion.

• After each period, players who reach their goal get a win.

• The first player to reach the target wins is the ultimate champion.

This is the single biggest driver of consistency — when a player has their own target, they show up.

**A few tips**

• You can set a challenge for one player, or for all of them at once.
Run a contest across the whole team so training becomes something they compare with each other.
Pick the level you want the team to reach. It gives the season a finish line.
Call out the players who trained, in front of the group. Recognition moves a team further than chasing does.
Nominate the player who put the work in. It is the cheapest motivation you have.
